info.title: HookPulse
info.description: Dead-man switch for webhooks/cron. Index: GET /api/.

bearerAuth.description: Guest token (`POST /api/guest`) in `X-Guest-Token: hp_…` or `Authorization: Bearer hp_…`. A `sess_…` session also works.

id.description: Monitor ID; it is the `:id` of the ingest URL.

name.description: Name you gave it, to recognise it in the alert.

interval_sec.description: Tolerated silence, in seconds. Past that, it is a miss.

alert_url.description: HTTPS URL that receives a POST on a miss (Slack, Discord, n8n).

last_event_at.description: Last ping received (UTC); `null` while it never pinged.

last_status.description: HTTP status the last ping sent, when it did.

last_latency_ms.description: Latency reported in the last ping, in ms.

miss_count.description: How many times this monitor has gone silent.

alerted_at.description: When the last alert went out — it is what holds the 1 alert/24h cap.

healthy.description: `true` when it has pinged at least once and is not overdue.

waiting_first_ping.description: `true` while it never pinged. Neither healthy nor overdue: nobody has wired it yet.

ingest_url.description: The URL your cron/webhook calls to prove life.

token.description: Read token of this monitor. Only comes on creation and to the owner.

status_url.description: Status of this monitor with the token already in the query.

events_url.description: Latest pings with the token already in the query.

curl_example.description: The ingest `curl`, ready to paste in the cron.

templates.description: Ingest snippets and the alert body, with this monitor already in them.

Monitor.description: A dead-man switch: the thing you make ping. If the ping stops for longer than `interval_sec`, it becomes `overdue` and the alert goes out.

ingest_curl.description: A `curl` that works as proof of life.

ingest_n8n.description: How to call the ingest from n8n.

miss_json.description: The exact JSON we POST to `alert_url` when the silence becomes a miss.

miss_url_hint.description: What works as `alert_url` — public HTTPS only.

Templates.description: How to ping and what we send when it fails. It is what saves guessing the format.

provider.description: Always `x402` — the only billing protocol accepted.

mode.description: Seller mode: `live` charges for real, `dev` lets calls through unpaid.

network.description: USDC network: `base` in production, `base-sepolia` in staging.

chain_id.description: EVM chain ID of the network above, so the wallet signs on the right chain.

homolog.description: Staging seam on: the loop can be closed without spending USDC.

dev_gate.description: How dev mode is unlocked, when it exists.

facilitator.description: URL of the facilitator that verifies and settles the payment.

asset_address.description: USDC contract on the network above.

wallets.description: Links to wallets that speak x402 (metamask, coinbase, base_app).

free_min_interval_sec.description: Shortest interval that is still free. Below it, it costs.

free_email_alerts.description: Free e-mail alert registrations; the rest is paid (it is SES cost per miss).

prices.description: What each paid action costs, in USD.

usage.description: How much of the allowance the owner has used.

trial.description: The account's trial, when there is a session.

Billing.description: Everything that decides whether the next call will cost: x402 configuration, allowance, prices and trial.

email_alert_usd.description: E-mail alert registration beyond the first.

Precos.description: Prices in force, in dollars. Read them here, not from the documentation.

active.description: Whether it is in force now.

granted.description: `true` when THIS call granted the trial.

Trial.description: The period without the usage paywall that confirming the e-mail grants. It is the alternative to paying.

ok.description: Always `true` — failure comes as a 4xx/5xx status, not as `ok:false`.

Ok.description: Write confirmation with no body of its own to return.

status.description: Status reported by the caller, when it did.

latency_ms.description: Latency reported by the caller, in ms.

Ping.description: A ping received at the ingest — the proof of life.

token.description: Feed token. Read-only: it does not create, change or delete.

rotated.description: `true` when this call rotated the token and invalidated the previous URL.

json.description: URL of the dashboard as JSON.

rss.description: URL of the same dashboard as RSS 2.0.

note.description: The warning that whoever has the link reads the dashboard.

Feed.description: The URLs of the owner's public dashboard, with the token just minted or rotated.

summary.description: The number you look at first.

endpoints.description: One row per monitor, with no secret at all.

_links.description: This dashboard as JSON, as RSS and the API index.

FeedStatus.description: The owner's whole status dashboard, addressable by URL. The token in the path IS the credential — whoever has the link, reads.

overdue.description: Active and silent beyond the interval.

all_ok.description: `true` only with at least one monitor, none overdue and none waiting for the first ping — one that never pinged does not count as healthy.

ResumoStatus.description: The set in numbers. `all_ok` is the field for an external monitor to check without understanding the rest.

id.description: Stable label of THIS dashboard, derived from the pair (feed token, monitor) — it is not the ingest id, and it changes when the owner rotates the token. The real id does not leave here because `GET /in/:id` asks for no credential: publishing it would give whoever only reads the power to reset the silence counter.

overdue.description: Whether it is silent beyond the interval.

alerts.description: Which alert channels are on: `{ email, url }` — booleans, never the address.

LinhaStatus.description: A monitor on the public dashboard: enough to know the state, with no token, no e-mail and no ingest id.

today_contacts.description: Contact messages received today. Only with `METRICS_TOKEN`: contact does not leave without a token.

days.description: One record per day of the window, with the counts of each metric.

usage.description: Usage per product resource — here, monitors.

financeiro.description: Aggregate of the day: `hoje_usd`, `hoje_count`, `rede`. Only with `METRICS_TOKEN`: money does not leave without a token; the full series is `payments`.

Metricas.description: 7-day panel. `payments` only shows with the operator token and only on Base mainnet.

post.summary: MCP server over HTTP (Streamable HTTP, JSON-RPC 2.0) — plugs into the client with nothing to install.
post.description:
The tools are the operations of this same catalog; the MCP has no backend of its own. `GET /mcp` returns the server card.
Returns: JSON-RPC 2.0 response (`initialize`, `tools/list` or `tools/call`).
Credentials go in the usual headers (X-Guest-Token, Authorization, X-PAYMENT) and are forwarded to the API.
An exhausted quota comes back as a 402 with accepts[] inside the tool result — pay and repeat.

post.summary: Creates a guest `hp_…` — it is the anonymous owner of your monitors.
post.description:
Keep the token: without it there is no way back to the monitors, unless you have already tied them to an e-mail.
Returns: { token }

post.summary: Creates a dead-man switch: silence beyond the interval becomes an alert.
post.description:
This response is the only one that shows the monitor's `token` and the `templates` — keep them. The second monitor, or an interval below the free minimum, answers **402 with `accepts[]`**: pay and repeat. A miss alerts at most once per 24h (or per interval, if it is longer).
Returns: { id, name, interval_sec, alert_to, alert_url, last_event_at, last_status, last_latency_ms, miss_count, alerted_at, active, healthy, overdue, waiting_first_ping, created_at, ingest_url, token?, status_url?, events_url?, curl_example?, templates?{ingest_curl,ingest_cron,ingest_n8n,miss_json,miss_url_hint} }

name.description: Name to recognise the monitor in the alert.

interval_sec.description: Tolerated silence, in seconds. Below the free minimum, it costs.

alert_to.description: E-mail to alert on a miss; without it, the account is alerted.

alert_url.description: Public HTTPS URL that receives a POST on a miss (Slack Incoming, Discord, n8n).

200.description: { id, name, interval_sec, alert_to, alert_url, last_event_at, last_status, last_latency_ms, miss_count, alerted_at, active, healthy, overdue, waiting_first_ping, created_at, ingest_url, token?, status_url?, events_url?, curl_example?, templates?{ingest_curl,ingest_cron,ingest_n8n,miss_json,miss_url_hint} }

post.summary: Talks to support: a human solves Turnstile, an agent pays $0.10 in x402.
post.description:
The first agent message is free; after that the backoff is 60s doubling up to a 1-hour cap, announced in `Retry-After`.
Returns: { ok, path }

name.description: What to call the person writing.

form_ts.description: When the form was opened; it is the anti-robot of the human path.

ok.description: Always `true` when the message was accepted.

path.description: Which path it came through: human with captcha or paid agent.

402.description: Quota exceeded. The response carries `accepts[]` (x402, USDC on Base): pay and repeat the same call with `X-PAYMENT`.

post.summary: Ping from the interface that increments the day's visits. Agents need not call it.
post.description:
Smoke does not count: `X-MM-Smoke`, User-Agent `mm-smoke` or `smoke: true` in the body come in as `counted: false`.
Returns: { ok, counted, reason? }

smoke.description: `true` marks the call as a test and it does not enter the count.

counted.description: Whether the visit entered the day's count.

reason.description: Why it did not count, when `counted` is `false`.

get.summary: Metrics of the last 7 days. With the operator token, includes payments.
get.description:
Without credentials it returns visits, usage and accounts. With `METRICS_TOKEN` as Bearer it adds `payments` — and only on Base mainnet, because staging numbers on a finance panel mislead.
Returns: { app, today, today_visits, today_contacts?, days, usage, accounts, financeiro?, payments? }

200.description: { app, today, today_visits, today_contacts?, days, usage, accounts, financeiro?, payments? }
